fatal_flaws: Nothing blocks the design outright. The most serious problem: A or B dropped on a water, cliff or nodata cell has no way out. Grid moves are forbidden when 'either end is impassable or nodata', and the design never snaps an endpoint, so a pin on a lakeshore cell or a steep ridge cell always returns 'unreachable'.

Serious: the finalize cron job passes '--prune --confirm' automatically every Sunday, and sync-trails runs --prune on every build. Both delete by B2 VersionId with no human in the loop. The repo convention is that deletion is manual-only behind an explicit --confirm (cli.py prune/cleanup-spread-frames, lines 1573-1586).
best_ideas: Takes the fire list from our own published catalogs/catalog.json, so no fire-API index traffic. The ids and acres match the site. I verified the live catalog has 321 fires with braced and bare cornea_ids (e.g. 4883092e-…), and fire_key normalization handles both.
bundle_id is a content hash of the build inputs. Anything that changes the inputs becomes a cheap 'check' that skips unchanged fires before doing any expensive work.

Offline trails come from an in-memory pmtiles BufferSource over a whole-file window.fetch of the per-fire extract. That needs no Range emulation, no exported packedFile/OPFS File handle and no invalidation on pack update. The national archive is never packed, so the wrapper's Range blindness (packs.ts:128-166) never matters.
OSM uses apt osmium-tool (tags-filter plus one multi-bbox extract -c) and a stdlib OPL parser. It keeps exact node-id topology with no PyPI dependency, which best matches the owner's preferences.
Pointers live only under catalogs/, so the existing 60 s must-revalidate rule (config.py CACHE_CONTROL_RULES) applies. Immutable assets go under versioned trails/ and routing/ prefixes.

Subcommands are registered from separate trails_cli.py and routing_cli.py via register(sub, common). common is a closure inside build_parser, which I verified, so the 1,598-line cli.py gets only one line.
Workflows copy tile.yml exactly (tee + PIPESTATUS + GITHUB_OUTPUT, 4-shard matrix, own concurrency group). Adds pytest guard steps and a dry_run dispatch that uploads the 3.8.4 output as an artifact.
pointer.pmtiles_url_s3 points at the S3 endpoint, whose 206 responses Chrome HTTP-caches (verified in the facts), with no extra VITE_ env plumbing.

Health goes to separate catalogs/health/{trails,routing}.json files, and HealthView reads the per-workflow runs endpoint. That avoids both the RMW race in health.publish (health.py:77-84) and the shared 40-run window (HealthView.tsx:29).
The trail popup handler bails if a higher-priority feature is under the tap (hotspots, fire pins, incidents), and also on an armed draw tool.
One 3-band UInt16 grid.tif, DEFLATE with PREDICTOR=2, serves both routing and the Vegetation layer.
A routing-one dev command plus a CI dry-run artifact covers GDAL 3.8.4 verification.

fatal_flaws: Nothing fatal. Most serious: off-trail and graph costs use the 3D length d3=√(dh²+dz²) divided by rates that are defined over horizontal distance (the Tobler, GET and Campbell convention). That inflates times by 1/cos θ, about +15% at 30°.

Serious: it rejects apt osmium-tool on the grounds that it 'loses per-vertex IDs'. That is inaccurate: OPL output keeps way node refs, as the pipeline design shows. The result is an avoidable PyPI dependency (pyosmium).
best_ideas:
The best offline field UX, including:
- Trails turn on automatically on the blank offline ground.
- The per-fire extract also carries an OSM 'ways' layer as a road reference.
- A dashed routing-area box.
- Drive and Apparatus show an explicit 'offline' mode state instead of the misleading 'No route found'.
Keeps each mode's error in modes[p] as {failed: WalkError}. Without that, the profile-switch path (SearchDirectionsControl.tsx:409-422) cannot show specific offroad error text.

Snaps an endpoint to walkable ground within 150 m (SNAP_MOVED note). When an endpoint is inside the perimeter, avoidance turns off for that route with a warning (ENDPOINT_IN_PERIM) rather than failing.
The A* search runs as a generator that yields every 40k settled nodes over a MessageChannel. A newer request marks the old one 'superseded', so marker drags stay responsive.
Per-query search arrays are window-local, which is much lighter on phone memory than full-grid arrays.
Conflation drops OSM trail chains that duplicate an agency trail (15 m / 80% rule). DEM elevation is smoothed along chains so 30 m noise doesn't inflate climb.

routing/index.json is built only from the per-fire pointers, one GET per active fire. No list API or B2 intermediates are needed, and a crashed shard can only leave orphan bundles, never a dangling pointer.
Pruning stays manual-only behind --confirm, as the repo convention requires.
The rd-route source carries no OSM attribution because TomTom and OSRM routes share it. The routing credit goes in the result card instead.
Uses the existing health.publish sections and documents the RMW race honestly.
Region-affine sharding: each Geofabrik region is downloaded by one shard per run. PBFs are deliberately not stored in actions/cache.

fatal_flaws: Nothing fatal. Most serious: the NHD actions/cache key includes github.run_id, so each of 4 shards saves a new ~0.4 GB cache on every daily run. On top of ~3.3 GB of weekly OSM caches, that will thrash the repo's 10 GB cache limit and evict the uv caches every workflow relies on.

Serious: the 100 km AOI cap produces about 11M cells at 30 m for Crosswhite, roughly 44 MB of decoded grids before any search arrays. That is a real phone-memory risk, only partly mitigated by capping the search window by deviceMemory.

Serious: routing publishes health.publish(storage, 'routing') into the shared catalogs/health.json from the routing-bundles concurrency group without acknowledging the read-modify-write race (health.py:77-84).
best_ideas: A Python reference A* (routing/validate.py) exports parity fixtures (costs plus cell/vertex sequences) that the TS A* must match, plus golden routes: Iron Creek→Stanley Lake with trail share ≥0.85, and Bob Marshall summit with an xc leg.
States the speed convention explicitly: rates apply over horizontal distance. It also proves the A* heuristic admissible (V_MAX=1.405 m/s, multipliers ≥1).
Checks storage.exists(done.json) before re-uploading an immutable part, which avoids creating hidden B2 versions (B2Storage.exists uses head_object).
Paints the vegetation layer from worker class bytes with the existing productRenderer buildLut/paintProduct (productRenderer.ts:66-129). That is the best reuse of repo code.
When routing with avoidance finds no path, it reruns without avoidance and returns 'blocked_by_perimeter' with the alternative route attached, which the user can opt into showing.
Simple region-affine sharding via crc32(primary_region) % shards. Fire keys are cornea_id.strip('{}').lower().
lf_epoch rebuilds grids automatically when LF2025 coverage expands (scheduled for Nov 2026).
Chooses GET v2 with a −2.8° peak shift, and applies Sullivan tertile ratios clamped to ±30°. That is the smallest defensible change that makes the cost anisotropic.

must_fix: Rebase onto origin/main before touching any contested file. Worktree base 69858dc is 8 commits behind (git log 69858dc..origin/main: 9ab4f1a/c40f05c dropped pin, 0f2239b NWCG draw renamed rd-draw-* ids, d070af0/4a66479 hotspot flames plus the ensureOrder rewrite). 'rd-trails-hit' must go into frontend/src/map/pinDrop.ts FEATURE_LAYERS unconditionally, since it is already on main. Otherwise a trail tap on an idle map both opens the popup and drops a pin.

Do not add the offroad bundle/perimeter/avoid key to SearchDirectionsControl's all-mode effect key. That effect (SearchDirectionsControl.tsx:374-407, keyed on endpointsKey :353) refetches drive and apparatus (TomTom) every time the routing index or latest perimeter resolves. Rerun only the hike profile when the Walk context changes.

Keep the error per mode, e.g. modes[p] = {failed: err}. The profile-switch path (SearchDirectionsControl.tsx:409-422) sees only 'failed' and would fall back to 'No route found — try different points.' instead of the offroad error text (field's approach).

Snap an A or B that falls on an impassable or nodata cell to the nearest walkable cell within about 150 m, and record a note. Pipeline's move rules ('either end is impassable or nodata') otherwise make those endpoints permanently unreachable.
Compute travel time over horizontal distance: t = d_h·M/v. Field's d3=√(dh²+dz²) double-counts slope, because the Sullivan, GET and Tobler rates are horizontal (research notes; model §4.5).

Perimeter avoidance should be a hard block (buffered mask) with explicit handling. If an endpoint is inside, turn avoidance off for that route with a warning. If there is no path, return blocked_by_perimeter plus an opt-in alternative. Don't use pipeline's silent soft ×50 penalty with a 0 m buffer.

Never run '--confirm' deletion from a cron. Worker convention: deletion commands are manual-only behind an explicit --confirm (cli.py prune/cleanup-spread-frames). Keep routing and trails prune manual (field, model), and recommend the B2 lifecycle rule for hidden versions in the README.

Health must not introduce a silent read-modify-write writer. health.publish does get_json then put_json on the shared catalogs/health.json (health.py:77-84), and catalogs.yml and mirror.yml write it from the worker-b2-writes group. Either use separate catalogs/health/{trails,routing}.json (pipeline) or document the cosmetic race explicitly (field). Also use the per-workflow runs endpoint, because HealthView pulls only 40 runs across all workflows (HealthView.tsx:29).

Do not key actions/cache on github.run_id (model's NHD cache). With per-shard OSM caches that exhausts the 10 GB repo cache and evicts uv caches. Cache NHD HU8 extracts in B2 work/ (NHD is frozen) or on a stable key.

Keep mutable pointers under catalogs/, which already has the 60 s must-revalidate rule (config.py CACHE_CONTROL_RULES). Add only immutable 'trails/' and 'routing/' rules plus content types for .tif, .gz and .pmtiles (none exist today; everything falls back to application/octet-stream). Never set ContentEncoding (b2.py _extra sets only ContentType and CacheControl).

The national PMTiles URL must never enter the pack index, or the wrapper must bypass requests that carry a Range header. packs.ts:128-166 ignores headers and serves whole-file 200s, which pmtiles FetchSource rejects. Also extend the opfs.ts:46 ext regex and packs.ts:82-88 contentTypeFor with gz and pmtiles, otherwise they are served as application/json.

Add worker: { format: 'es' } to frontend/vite.config.ts, which currently has no worker key (a geotiff-importing module worker fails under iife, verified). Create the Worker lazily as a module singleton because of StrictMode double effects and vitest imports.

store.ts selectFire rebuilds the entire directions object ({a,b,profile,route,armed,picking}, :369-372). Carry directions.avoidPerimeter there and in clearDirections, and add the new layer slices to urlState.test.ts mkState or buildSearch throws.

Loaders outside React Query (routing index, descriptor, bundle buffers) must wait for or retry after pack hydration. main.tsx:41 calls initOfflinePacks without awaiting it, so offline requests issued before hydration go to the network and fail.

Reuse the existing code instead of writing new: spread/productRenderer buildLut/paintProduct for vegetation colours, spread/utm.ts utmBoundsTo4326 (add only a forward lonLatToUtm), and a toaBands-style shared vegClasses table. Keep LayerContext unchanged by using self-subscribing managers (basemapUnderlay.ts:121-131 pattern with the dead-map guard).

Use apt osmium-tool plus a stdlib OPL parser (pipeline) rather than PyPI pyosmium, and use GDAL ESRIJSON auto-paging with a returnCountOnly check (field, model) rather than a custom ArcGIS pager. Both choices are verified to work and minimize new code and dependencies.

fatal_flaws: Nothing fatal as written. The biggest correctness bug is the LF2025 rule (§3.6 step 1): it switches to LF2024 only when more than 95% of EVT pixels are −9999. LF2025 covers only the SW and NW GeoAreas until Nov 2026 (data-api-facts). A fire straddling a GeoArea boundary would therefore keep LF2025 with a large nodata share, and that ground falls into 'unknown veg ×4' (M[LF==0]=4.0). Use a per-pixel mosaic or a strict threshold.

TNM HU8 lookup (§3.6 step 3) uses max=50 without prodFormats=GeoPackage. Every product comes in 3 formats, and the captured response lists national, then state, then HU4, then HU8 items. A large AOI that spans two states can therefore silently lose HU8s, i.e. lose streams, to truncation. The 'HU) 8' title match itself is correct: 12 of 29 items in the captured tnm_nhd.json match.

The pace-code scale tops out at code 254 = 0.8·640 = 512 s/m, not the 377 the design states. Tree×TL×SB×stream at 45° needs about 753 s/m, so those cells are clipped and their time is under-reported if a route is ever forced through them. This is minor.
The fire list comes from the prod /fires?active=true on a new 3-hourly cron. Owner memory says prod fire-api is for live-site traffic only; published catalogs/catalog.json gives the same list.
health.publish is a read-modify-write of catalogs/health.json (health.py:77-84), called here from outside worker-b2-writes. The design accepts this race; separate health docs avoid it.

The PMTiles guard 'max_tile_bytes < 480k' cannot detect degradation. GDAL 3.8.4 keeps tiles at or under MAX_SIZE by silently halving EXTENT and dropping features, so degraded tiles pass. Count the CPL_DEBUG MVT lines instead.
best_ideas: Off-trail uses the GET v2 isotropic rate on TERRAIN slope (SlpD) times a round-trip-preserving asymmetry α(θ). I verified α(±15°)=1.104/0.896 and α(30°)=1.100. This is the only design that penalizes sidehill travel the way GET does.
Endpoint snapping: a spiral search to the nearest passable, unmasked cell within 150 m, with a SNAP_MOVED note. Without it, a pin on a >45° or water cell returns a false 'no route'.

Perimeter is a hard block with a 60 m dilation, applied to grid cells AND graph nodes. When an endpoint is inside it, avoidance turns off with an ENDPOINT_IN_PERIM warning. On no-path, the UI offers 'Try without perimeter avoidance'.
Safety notes: PERIM_OLD (perimeter over 12 h old), HOTSPOT_NEAR (a VIIRS/MODIS detection under 12 h old within 500 m), ONLINE_NO_PERIM, CROSSES_PERIM on online routes, and GAP_UNTIMED.
The per-fire PMTiles extract carries an OSM 'ways' layer. Offline there is no basemap, so roads and tracks are the crew's only ground reference. Trails switch on automatically on the offline ground.
Explicit offline states for drive and apparatus ('Needs a connection') instead of today's generic 'No route found'.
Memory-conscious worker: search arrays are window-local, and the A* is a sliced generator that stops when a newer request arrives (superseded). Data arrays stay at or under 25 MB even at 6.25M cells.
Mega-fire fallback: 60 m cells with a COARSE_GRID note, so the whole fire stays routable offline instead of being clipped.
Range-bypass hardening in the window.fetch wrapper, plus app-side recipe gating ('needs app update').
'Walk here' popup action, and a dashed routing-area box shown while Walk is active.

fatal_flaws: Perimeter avoidance is effectively broken on the network. §4.6 applies PERIM_PENALTY only under 'Grid moves', and the network sub-edge cost has no perimeter term. crossesPerimeter is only set by grid moves. So a route can follow a trail or road straight through the latest perimeter with no penalty and no warning.

The perimeter is a ×50 soft block with a 0 m buffer. When the route crosses, the UI says 'Route enters the latest perimeter — no way around was found', which can be false: a detour that costs more than 50× the crossing does exist. Use a hard block, a standoff buffer, and an explicit alternative.

No endpoint snapping. 'Start = A's cell', and moves out of an impassable cell are forbidden. Portals in impassable cells get no link either. A crew standing on a cell classed >45° (1.26% of the Stanley cells, clustered in exactly the steep terrain crews work) or on a lake-edge water cell gets 'No passable route found'.

The NHD HU8 filter matches nothing. It keeps titles containing 'Hydrologic Unit (HU) 8' or 'HU8', but the real titles read '…for Hydrological Unit (HU) 8 - 17050111…' (0 of 29 captured items match either string). Every bundle would silently lose perennial streams, NHD lakes and rivers, and nothing flags it.

Off-trail slope uses directional grade, θ=atan((z_to−z_from)/L) in vGet(|θ|), not terrain slope. Contouring across a 35° timbered sidehill is timed at about 58 min/km against GET's 182 min/km: 3× optimistic, and routes will favour steep sidehills.
best_ideas: The fire list comes from our own published catalogs/catalog.json, so the cron adds zero fire-API traffic. Perimeters come from DEV.
Separate catalogs/health/{trails,routing}.json docs, each with one writer. This avoids the health.json read-modify-write race.

bundle_id is a sha256 of the canonical inputs, including an AOI-scoped trails_hash and osm_hash. A 'check' action skips the rebuild when nothing inside the AOI changed. Rebuilds are idempotent and self-healing (a descriptor-exists check, then re-emitting the pointer).
The plan stage makes one osmium tags-filter plus one multi-bbox extract pass per region and uploads per-fire extracts to work/osm. Build shards never download state PBFs.
Lakes are perennial only: the NHDFCode join excludes intermittent and ephemeral waterbodies, so dry playas are not impassable. TNM uses prodFormats=GeoPackage.
ArcGIS paging is done in Python with count verification before and after, and a retry on mismatch.
Trails have a sanity gate: count floors plus a check against 0.9 of the previous build.
The offline trails extract is fetched whole through window.fetch into an in-memory pmtiles BufferSource. That needs no Range emulation, no OPFS File invalidation and no new packs.ts export.
The worker verifies sha256 before decode. Pruning is version-aware for B2 (delete by VersionId), and a test_config invariant guards the immutable prefixes.
The national PMTiles is read from the S3-endpoint URL, so Chrome HTTP-caches the 206 responses. CPL_DEBUG=MVT degradation lines are counted into health.
Gap legs are 'not timed', the modeled label is persistent, and legs are treated as fully correlated for the range totals.

fatal_flaws: The NHD HU8 filter matches nothing: it has the same 'Hydrologic Unit (HU) 8' / 'HU8' title test as pipeline (0 of 29 captured items). Streams and water would be silently lost unless the implementer happens to parse downloadURL.

The off-trail GET term uses directional grade, v_xc(θ)=v_GET(θ−θ0) with θ taken from the DEM difference. That makes sidehill travel up to 3× optimistic, even though the design says it follows GET's calibrated SlpD rule for the mask.

AOIs go up to 100 km: Crosswhite is about 11M cells, 44 MB of grids plus up to 6M-cell search windows. The design gates on navigator.deviceMemory, which Safari/iOS does not expose. That is a real phone OOM or jetsam risk, and there is no graceful 'oom' path.

A daily routing cron plus workflow_run, with crons observed slipping 3–6 h, means new or fast-growing fires can wait more than 24 h for an offline bundle. That lands in the first operational periods, when crews need it most.
3DEP exportImage is requested directly in UTM (bboxSR/imageSR=326zz). Only 5070 was verified. This is a secondary risk.
best_ideas: Per-pixel LF2025/LF2024 mosaic, applied consistently across EVT, EVC and FBFM40. It is the correct handling of partial LF2025 coverage.

Perimeter is a hard block with a 100 m standoff. If no path exists, the search re-runs without avoidance and returns 'blocked_by_perimeter' with the alternative route shown only on explicit user request.

The validation gate: a Python reference A* with a cross-language parity fixture, and golden routes (Sawtooth Iron Creek→Stanley Lake; Bob Marshall summit) with acceptance bands, plus an uphill-slower anisotropy check.
Conflation keeps OSM topology and transfers agency names and numbers onto covered OSM edges, using a bearing test so perpendicular crossings don't count as coverage.
OSM sac_scale T5/T6 (alpine climbing) and via_ferrata are excluded from crew routes. Poor trail_visibility gets a multiplier of at least 1.0, which keeps A* admissible.
Range-first summary: fast–slow in bold, typical secondary, plus 'Crew routing uses all trails regardless of these restrictions' in the popup.
An online route is checked against the latest perimeter on the main thread and warns when it crosses.
AOIs snap to a 3 km lattice and only grow, so small perimeter changes don't force rebuilds. Grid and graph carry an aoi_id pair check.

must_fix: NHD HU8 discovery. Match the substring '(HU) 8' or parse '_HU8_' from downloadURL, pass prodFormats=GeoPackage, and check total against max (or paginate). If a CONUS AOI returns zero HU8s, raise the nhd_unavailable warning; never proceed silently. Evidence: in scratchpad/dataapi/tnm_nhd.json the titles read '…for Hydrological Unit (HU) 8 - 17050111…'. Zero of 29 items contain 'Hydrologic Unit (HU) 8' or 'HU8' (pipeline line 552, model line 451). The captured list orders national, state, HU4, then HU8, so max=50 truncation hits HU8 first (field line 441 has no prodFormats).

The off-trail GET v2 slope term must use TERRAIN slope (LF2020 SlpD) so sidehill travel is penalized. Use directional grade only for the uphill/downhill asymmetry, as field does. Evidence: pipeline §4.6 uses θ=atan((z_to−z_from)/L) in vGet(|θ|), and model §4.5 uses v_xc=v_GET(θ−θ0). Contouring across a 35° timbered slope then costs 58 min/km against GET's 182 min/km (computed).

Perimeter avoidance must cover graph vertices and edges as well as grid cells. It needs a non-zero standoff (60–100 m) and a hard block. When blocked, show an explicit 'route through perimeter' alternative (model's blocked_by_perimeter), not a ×50 soft cost with a possibly false 'no way around was found' message. Evidence: pipeline design line 1064 applies the penalty only under 'Grid moves', and line 1083 sets 'Buffer 0 m'.

Endpoint snapping. When A's or B's cell is impassable (SlpD >45°, water, nodata), search for the nearest passable, unmasked cell within about 150 m and add a flagged connector and note. Otherwise steep-terrain pins return a false 'unreachable': 1.26% of Stanley cells are >45° (data-api-facts). The pipeline has no snapping: 'Start = A's cell', and moves out of blocked cells are forbidden.

LF2025/LF2024 selection. Use model's per-pixel mosaic across EVT, EVC and FBFM40 together, or pipeline's strict ≤0.1% nodata rule. Do not use field's '>95% nodata' switch, which leaves fires straddling a GeoArea boundary with large unknown-veg areas. LF2025 covers only the SW and NW GeoAreas until Nov 2026 (data-api-facts; field line 432).

Offline pack consistency on flaky networks. The mutable routing index or descriptor is fetched network-first and may point to a newer bundle that is not in the pack. If a bundle file then fails, retry from the pack's snapshot bundle (for example PackMeta.routingBundle). Also serve IMMUTABLE packed URLs pack-first even while navigator.onLine is true. Otherwise every step (index → descriptor → grid → graph) can wait NETWORK_PATIENCE_MS=8000 on dead Wi-Fi (packs.ts wrapper: network-first with an 8 s race only for packed URLs).

Online fallback routes (ORS/Valhalla) must be tested against the latest perimeter and must warn: ONLINE_NO_PERIM always, CROSSES_PERIM on a crossing. Untimed dashed end-gap legs must be kept, because online engines snap endpoints up to 35 km. The pipeline annotates only 'online engine used'.

Headline time for modeled Walk routes. The mode button and summary lead must show the range, or the slow (low-tertile) bound, not only '~typical'. This follows IRPG 'time with the slowest person' and Sullivan's advice to use the low tertile for a slow or injured member. All three designs put '~typical' on the mode button (SearchDirectionsControl.tsx per-mode label).

Phone memory. Cap 30 m grids at about 6M cells, keep search arrays window-local, and do not rely on navigator.deviceMemory, which Safari/iOS lacks. Coarsen to 60 m with a COARSE_GRID note rather than shipping 11M-cell 100 km AOIs (model §3.7). Mid-range Android and iPhone timings are an explicit pre-release gate; no phone timings exist in the research.

Health reporting. Do not call health.publish from the new workflows' concurrency groups: health.py:77-84 read-modify-writes catalogs/health.json, which worker-b2-writes jobs also write. Use separate catalogs/health/{trails,routing}.json docs (pipeline) and HealthView rows backed by the per-workflow runs endpoint (HealthView.tsx:29 fetches only the latest 40 runs).

Fire list for the routing cron. Read the published catalogs/catalog.json, or use FIRE_API_DEV, not prod /fires?active=true, per owner memory ('prod fire-api is for live-site traffic only'). Perimeters come from FIRE_API_DEV with verbatim paths.
Offline drive and apparatus modes. SearchDirectionsControl fetches every profile in parallel (lines 381-388). Offline they must show 'Needs a connection', not 'No route found — try different points.'

Crew-inappropriate OSM ways. Exclude or hard-block sac_scale T5/T6 (demanding/difficult alpine) and highway=via_ferrata as model does. Field's exclusion list omits via_ferrata, and pipeline only multiplies T5/T6 by 2.5 or 4.

Water barriers. Treat only perennial NHD waterbodies as impassable, excluding fcode 39001/39005/39006 via the NHDFCode join, as pipeline does. Field and model mark all LakePond/Reservoir polygons impassable, which creates false barriers at dry playas.

GDAL 3.8.4 PMTiles degradation detection. Count CPL_DEBUG=MVT reduction lines and record them in health. A 'max tile < 480 kB' check cannot see degradation, because GDAL keeps tiles at or under MAX_SIZE by silently halving EXTENT and dropping features (tiles-infra-facts).
